questions.q: What does Azure Databricks manage for you, compared to running Spark yourself?
options: Provisioning, configuring, and tearing down the actual cluster of machines that runs Spark
Writing all of your PySpark code automatically
Only the storage layer, never any compute
Nothing — Databricks is unrelated to Spark
questions.explain: Someone still has to provision machines, install Spark, and keep versions compatible — Databricks does that for you.

questions.q: What problem does a traditional data lake struggle with, that a data warehouse handles well?
options: Transactions, schema guarantees, and fast point lookups
Storing large volumes of raw files cheaply
Flexibility in what data formats can be stored
Data lakes have no weaknesses compared to warehouses
questions.explain: A data lake is cheap and flexible but weak on exactly the guarantees a database is good at.

options: Cheap object storage (a data lake) combined with transactional guarantees (Delta Lake) layered on top
A data warehouse that has been converted entirely into unstructured files
A synonym for Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 with no other meaning
A physical building where Databricks servers are housed
questions.explain: This is Databricks' core pitch, and Chapter 2 of this course explains how Delta Lake actually delivers those guarantees.

questions.q: How does this course relate to Data Engineering Foundations?
options: It builds directly on Foundations' Spark and PySpark material — Databricks is the platform that code actually runs on in the real world
It replaces everything learned in Foundations with a completely different technology
It has no connection to Foundations at all
It only covers material already fully covered in Foundations, with nothing new
questions.explain: Every line of Foundations' PySpark code ran implicitly against some Spark cluster — this course is about that cluster.

questions.q: What is Delta Lake, at a high level?
options: A table format that adds transactional guarantees on top of files stored in object storage
A completely separate cloud storage service unrelated to Azure Data Lake Storage
A programming language for writing Spark jobs
A replacement for Unity Catalog
questions.explain: This is exactly the piece that makes the lakehouse idea work — Chapter 2 covers it in full.
